title: Are the Frequencies All Different?

concept.title: A set of the counts
body: First count how often each value occurs (a map from value to count). The question is whether **all these counts are different**. The counts are numbers too, so put them into a set: if the set has as many elements as the map has entries, no two values had the same count.
Using one hash structure on the output of another is a common pattern: count first, then examine the counts.

statement: Print `yes` if every value of the array occurs a different number of times than every other value, otherwise print `no`.

examples.note: 1 occurs 3 times, 2 twice and 3 once: all different.

hints: Count how often each value occurs.
Put the counts into a set.
The answer is yes when the set has the same size as the number of different values.

explanation: The counts are collected in a set. A smaller set than the number of values means that two values had the same count.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
for x in a:
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
print("yes" if len(set(count.values())) == len(count) else "no")
